title: Game Programming & Design
description: Build in Unity. Understand the logic. Test your ideas.
alignmentNote: The six Essentials units follow Unity’s educator outline in mission order. Each is a classroom companion with original notes, a small C# exercise, Unity activities, and a checkpoint—not a replacement for every Unity Learn tutorial. Junior Programmer follows Essentials. Console exercises run separately from Unity scene scripts.

units.title: Editor Essentials
units.summary: Unity Essentials mission 1: navigate the Editor and compose a mural.

lessons.title: Find your way around a scene

exercise.title: Name the practice arena
exercise.prompt: Inside GetArenaName(), create a string variable named arenaName containing "Practice Arena". Return arenaName. Keep Main so you can see the result in a C# compiler.
hints: Use double quotes for the text.
Declare the string, then return the variable.

unityTask: Complete the installation and project-opening steps in the Unity Learn companion.
Complete the Scene-view navigation and flying-test activities.
Design the mural in the supplied scene. Save, enter Play mode, then stop and describe which edits persisted.

questions.prompt: Where do you inspect components on a selected GameObject?
questions.explanation: The Inspector displays components and their editable settings for the selection.

questions.prompt: Which view is used to arrange the world rather than see the camera output?
questions.explanation: Scene view is the editing workspace. Game view displays what the game cameras render.

questions.prompt: You move an ordinary scene object during Play mode, then stop. What should you normally expect?
choices: The change is saved to every scene
The edit is not retained after Play mode
The editor cannot exit Play mode
questions.explanation: Make lasting ordinary scene edits outside Play mode and save the scene.

questions.prompt: What does return do in the practice method?
choices: Sends a value back to its caller
questions.explanation: Returning a value and printing it are separate operations.

units.title: 3D Essentials
units.summary: Unity Essentials mission 2: furnish a room, test physics, and use prefab blocks.

lessons.title: GameObjects, components, and changing values

exercise.title: Move a practice marker
exercise.prompt: Return x + distance as a float. Negative distances move in the opposite direction. Do not use UnityEngine in this console exercise.
hints: Both inputs already have the right numeric type.
Return an expression using both parameters.

unityTask: Arrange furniture in the supplied kid’s bedroom. Adjust Transform values outside Play mode.
Create a ball with a Collider and Rigidbody; test its bounce with a physics material.
Create a prefab block and build a tower from instances. Adjust the room’s lighting, background, and camera, then save and test.

lessons.title: Prefab instances and scoring arithmetic

exercise.title: Score a pickup batch
exercise.prompt: Return the existing score plus coins multiplied by pointsPerCoin. Inputs are nonnegative whole numbers. A batch of zero coins leaves the score unchanged.
exercise.signature: int CalculateScore(int score, int coins, int pointsPerCoin)
hints: Calculate earned points from coins and pointsPerCoin.
Add earned points to the existing score.

unityTask: Compare a prefab asset with two instances in the scene.
Change an instance, then explain what changes when you edit the prefab asset instead.
Run the score rule for two different block counts and record the returned values.

questions.prompt: Which component makes a 3D object participate in physics simulation?
questions.explanation: A Rigidbody adds physics simulation; a Collider supplies a collision shape.

questions.prompt: What is a prefab asset?
questions.explanation: A prefab is a reusable template from which you can create instances.

units.title: Audio Essentials
units.summary: Unity Essentials mission 3: create and test an immersive soundscape.

lessons.title: Build a soundscape and adjust volume

exercise.title: Build a soundscape and adjust volume
exercise.prompt: Return volume multiplied by gain. Inputs are between 0 and 1; no clamping is needed.
hints: Use the multiplication operator, *.
Return a numeric value rather than writing sound-playing code.

unityTask: Complete Create an immersive soundscape in the Unity Learn kitchen scene.
Use at least one looping sound and compare 2D with 3D spatial behavior.
Move the listener and explain how distance changes the sound.

questions.prompt: Which component emits audio?
questions.explanation: AudioSource emits sound; AudioListener receives it.

questions.prompt: What should you test for a 3D AudioSource?
questions.explanation: Spatial sound depends on the position of the source and listener.

units.title: Programming Essentials
units.summary: Unity Essentials mission 4: move a character, rotate an object, and collect it.

lessons.title: Scripts, methods, and a tiny game loop

exercise.title: Calculate a frame’s travel distance
exercise.prompt: Return speed * elapsedSeconds. speed is units per second and elapsedSeconds is seconds. Both inputs are nonnegative. A paused interval of zero seconds produces zero distance.
hints: Keep both quantities in the same unit system.
Multiply; do not add speed and time.

unityTask: Complete Add a movement script in the supplied living room. Identify Start and Update.
Create a rotating collectible and test its motion.
Complete Collect the collectible. Add a Console message to confirm collection, then explain what the message tells you.

questions.prompt: Why multiply a speed by elapsed seconds?
choices: To calculate a distance for that interval
To convert a bool to text
To make every computer have the same frame rate
questions.explanation: Speed times elapsed time gives distance; it does not force a specific frame rate.

questions.prompt: Which description best fits Update in an active enabled MonoBehaviour?
choices: Once when the project is saved
questions.explanation: Update is a per-frame callback. Start is used for initial setup.

units.title: 2D Essentials
units.summary: Unity Essentials mission 5: build a 2D puzzle scene and animate a pet.

lessons.title: Work in a 2D scene

exercise.title: Work in a 2D scene
exercise.prompt: Return the new x coordinate after adding offset to x.
hints: Use addition.
Return x + offset.

unityTask: Complete Set up a 2D room and Complete your 2D Puzzle Game in the Unity companion.
Identify a SpriteRenderer, the camera, and a 2D physics component in your scene.
Complete Add an animated pet. Explain how frames, the animation clip, and Animator relate.

questions.prompt: Which pair belongs to the 2D physics system?
questions.explanation: Use the 2D component family together for 2D physics.

questions.prompt: What does a sprite animation clip contain?
questions.explanation: A sequence of sprite frames changes the displayed image over time.

units.title: Publishing Essentials
units.summary: Unity Essentials mission 6: build, test, document, and share your portfolio project.

lessons.title: Build, test, and share a project

exercise.title: Build, test, and share a project
exercise.prompt: Return the text "Project: " followed by title. Include the space after the colon.
hints: Use + to join the prefix and title.
Return "Project: " + title.

unityTask: Complete Build your portfolio project and Publish to WebGL using the companion instructions for your Editor.
Complete the bonus-scene challenge and capture a video showing your game.
Share through the approved classroom destination. Verify the link, controls, and credits on another device.

questions.prompt: What is a necessary test before sharing a web build?
choices: Run the built version through supported hosting
questions.explanation: The packaged game must be tested separately from Editor Play mode.

questions.prompt: What should you check if your build opens the wrong scene?
choices: The included scenes and starting scene
questions.explanation: The build must include the intended scenes and start with the correct one.

units.title: Junior Programmer: player control & game rules
units.summary: Translate movement, boundaries, spawning permission, and life changes into testable C#.
units.pathway: Junior Programmer · Player Control / Basic Gameplay

lessons.title: Steer with inputs and frame time

exercise.title: Calculate the next player position
exercise.prompt: Return x + input * speed * elapsedSeconds. Input is between -1 and 1; speed and elapsedSeconds are nonnegative. Do not clamp the result in this lesson.
exercise.signature: float CalculateHorizontalPosition(float x, float input, float speed, float elapsedSeconds)
hints: Compute displacement before adding the original position.
Preserve the sign of input.

unityTask: Follow Player Control and identify the variable controlling speed.
Predict the effect of doubling speed, test it, and restore the original value.
Explain why a camera needs a suitable position and viewing direction to show the player.

lessons.title: Keep a player inside the arena

exercise.title: Clamp a player position
exercise.prompt: Return x clamped to the inclusive interval [min, max]. The bounds are valid and may be negative. Use comparisons and if statements; no Unity APIs are needed.
exercise.signature: float ClampPlayerPosition(float x, float min, float max)
hints: Check the lower edge and upper edge separately.
If neither condition applies, return the original position.

unityTask: Add or locate the boundary checks in your Player Control project.
Test both edges and describe whether the project clamps, freezes, or removes an object.
Record a bug, the input that reveals it, and the change that fixes it.

lessons.title: Gate an action with game state

exercise.title: Decide whether a player can fire
exercise.prompt: Return true only when pressed is true, gameOver is false, and remaining <= 0f. A negative remaining value is ready. Return a bool, not the text "true".
exercise.signature: bool CanFireProjectile(bool pressed, bool gameOver, float remaining)
hints: All three conditions must be satisfied.
Use !gameOver to require the game to still be active.

unityTask: In Basic Gameplay, identify the prefab and the code that creates an instance.
Explain why spawning every Update without a gate would create many projectiles.
Describe how you would prevent shooting after game over.

lessons.title: Collisions, lives, and debugging a rule

exercise.title: Update remaining lives
exercise.prompt: Given nonnegative lives, subtract one only when hit is true and at least one life remains. Never return a negative value. If there is no hit, keep the value unchanged.
hints: Use && to combine a hit with having lives left.
Keep the existing lives in every other situation.

unityTask: Demonstrate one collision or trigger interaction in your prototype.
Explain whether that interaction should physically block the other object.
Test zero lives and explain how gameplay stops or changes state.

questions.prompt: Which description best fits Update in an active enabled MonoBehaviour?
choices: Once when the project is saved
questions.explanation: Update is a per-frame callback. Start is used for initial setup.

questions.prompt: A signed input of -1 usually represents what in our horizontal rule?
choices: Movement in the opposite direction from +1
questions.explanation: The negative sign reverses the displacement direction.

questions.prompt: A clamped player is exactly at the maximum boundary. What happens to that coordinate?
questions.explanation: Inclusive boundaries allow values exactly on either edge.

questions.prompt: Which operator compares two values for equality?
questions.explanation: == asks whether values are equal. = performs assignment.

questions.prompt: pressed is true, gameOver is false, and remaining is 0.2. Can our player fire?
choices: Yes, because the button is pressed
questions.explanation: All three requirements must be satisfied; remaining must be zero or below.

questions.prompt: What does instantiation do in the spawning workflow?
choices: Creates an instance from a template
questions.explanation: Instantiation creates an object instance at runtime.

questions.prompt: Why choose a trigger for a collectible?
choices: To detect overlap without physically blocking the player
questions.explanation: A trigger reports overlap instead of acting as an ordinary blocking collision surface.

questions.prompt: Lives decrease twice on one pickup. What is a useful first investigation?
choices: Count how often the event handler runs
questions.explanation: Repeated events can cause repeated state updates. Observe the calls before changing the rule.
